# isocountry

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/m-muecke/isocountry/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/m-muecke/isocountry/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![CRAN status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/isocountry)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=isocountry)
[![R-universe version](https://m-muecke.r-universe.dev/isocountry/badges/version)](https://m-muecke.r-universe.dev/isocountry)
<!-- badges: end -->

isocountry provides ISO country, currency, and market identifier codes as plain data frames, with no
dependencies.

## Datasets

- `isocountry`: [ISO 3166-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1) country codes with
  [UN M49](https://unstats.un.org/unsd/methodology/m49/overview) regions and membership in the OECD,
  the European Union (EU), the euro area (EMU), and the European Economic Area (EEA).
- `isocurrency`:
  [ISO 4217](https://www.six-group.com/en/products-services/financial-information/data-standards.html)
  currency codes with minor units and the countries using each currency.
- `isocurrency_historic`: withdrawn ISO 4217 currency codes, e.g. the national currencies replaced
  by the euro.
- `isomic`: [ISO 10383](https://www.iso20022.org/market-identifier-codes) market identifier codes
  (MICs) for exchanges and other trading venues.

Across the datasets, `country_code` is the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (`alpha_2` in `isocountry`) and
`country_number` is the numeric code, so the datasets join easily. Use `tibble::as_tibble()` or
`data.table::as.data.table()` if you prefer tibbles or data.tables.

## Installation

You can install the released version of isocountry from [CRAN](https://CRAN.R-project.org) with:

```{r}
#| eval: false
install.packages("isocountry")
```

And the development version from [GitHub](https://github.com/m-muecke/isocountry) with:

```{r}
#| eval: false
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("m-muecke/isocountry")
```

## Usage

```{r}
library(isocountry)
```

Look up a country:

```{r}
subset(
  isocountry,
  alpha_2 == "DE",
  c(name, alpha_3, country_number, region_name, eu_member, emu_member)
)
```

List the euro area members:

```{r}
isocountry$name[isocountry$emu_member]
```

Find the countries using a currency:

```{r}
subset(isocurrency, currency_code == "CHF", c(country_name, country_code))
```

Look up exchanges by their MIC:

```{r}
subset(isomic, mic %in% c("XNYS", "XLON", "XETR"), c(mic, market_name, country_code))
```

Add the currencies to the countries:

```{r}
countries <- merge(
  isocountry[c("alpha_2", "name", "region_name")],
  isocurrency[c("country_code", "currency_code", "currency_name")],
  by.x = "alpha_2",
  by.y = "country_code"
)
head(countries)
```

## Related work

- [countrycode](https://github.com/vincentarelbundock/countrycode): R package to convert country
  names and codes between coding schemes
- [ISOcodes](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=ISOcodes): R package with ISO language, country,
  currency, script, and character codes, and UN M49 area codes

isocountry is inspired by the
[ISO-3166-Countries-with-Regional-Codes](https://github.com/lukes/ISO-3166-Countries-with-Regional-Codes)
project.
